Hi Jane / Tom 

Thanks again for the call today  really helpful to hear the team context and the three primary success levers you called out (safety, latency at 95th, and reduction in cost per API call). Per our discussion, I'm attaching a first-pass POC plan that captures: success criteria, timeline, owners, and a light eval approach (offline + shadow).

Quick recap / asks:
- Success criteria: 1) <5% critical hallucinations on intent classification tasks; 2) median latency <120ms and p95 <300ms; 3) end-to-end cost reduction >= 30% vs current baseline for the user flows we discussed.
- Evaluation approach: we recommended a two-part eval: offline datasets for deterministic scoring + 2-week online shadow run on 1% of traffic to validate latency and degradation under real load.
- Next steps: please confirm (a) stakeholders for test data and shadow access (we need an owner for production sampling), (b) timeline constraints (is the week of Mar 8 good for kickoff?), and (c) whether SOC2 artifacts / security questionnaire items need to be included in the initial handoff.

Attached: acme-poc-plan-v1.pdf (POC plan draft) and a small sample dataset. I've looped in Rachel to propose an eval rubric and connor for CS/ops ownership.

Thanks 
Marissa

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FW: Follow-up and POC evaluation plan - Acme POC

Hi team 

Draft rubric and methodology below (high level) that we can share with Acme. I kept it lean so legal/security can review quickly.

1) Offline eval
- Dataset: combined set of 2k labeled examples across the 5 target intents (Acme-supplied + augmentation).
- Metrics: Exact-match for classification/intent (EM), F1 for slot extraction, BLEU/ROUGE not required for this task. For hallucination: use "unsupported_response_rate" (responses containing hallucinated facts per manual annotation sample).
- Thresholds: pass = EM >= 92% on intent; hallucination rate <= 5% (critical hallucinations <= 1%).

2) Online shadow (recommended after passing offline):
- Traffic: 1% sampled production traffic or replayed requests for 2 weeks.
- Observability: p50/p95 latency, error rate, token cost per successful call; capture top 10 error traces.
- Rollout guardrails: automatic rollback if p95 latency increases >2x baseline or error rate >1%.

3) Grading rubric (one-page summary to customer):
- Safety: Critical = any user-impacting hallucination -> FAIL; Minor = non-user-impacting deviations -> score penalty.
- Quality: Intent EM score mapped to grade A/B/C with cutoffs (A >= 95, B 92-95, C <92).
- Performance: p95 latency target <300ms (A), 300-450ms (B), >450ms (C).
- Cost: Target cost reduction >=30% to qualify as pass.

Owners:
- Rachel Kim (redwood): Eval dataset, offline scoring pipeline, grading rubric (rachel_kim@redwood.com)
- Connor O'Brien (redwood): Shadow rollout plan, sampling script, infra access for logs (connor_obrien@redwood.com)
- Marissa: Customer PM liaison and final decision maker for success criteria.

I'll draft a single-page rubric PDF and upload to the Drive link. Let me know if you want stricter thresholds; I erred on the conservative side to reduce rework.

-Rachel
Rachel Kim | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com
